goal: Arduino Uno night light: a photoresistor (LDR) and a 10k resistor as a voltage divider into A0, and a white or yellow 5 mm LED on D9 through a 220 ohm resistor that turns on when the room gets dark.

plan.title: Automatic Night Light with Photoresistor and LED
plan.summary: This project creates an automatic night light using an Arduino Uno, a light-dependent resistor (photoresistor), and a yellow LED. The photoresistor measures ambient light levels, and when the room gets dark, the Arduino automatically turns on the LED.
plan.final_result: When powered on via USB, the Arduino monitors ambient room light through the photoresistor. In bright light, the yellow LED remains off. When you cover the photoresistor with your hand or darken the room, the yellow LED turns on automatically like a night light.
safety: Always disconnect the USB cable before placing or modifying wires and components.
Make sure the 220 ohm resistor is always in series with the LED to avoid drawing too much current and damaging the Arduino pin or LED.
Ensure no bare wire ends or component leads touch each other accidentally.

parts.why: Provides a solderless surface to plug in all components and connect them neatly.

part_guide.bb: A full-size solderless breadboard with numbered rows and tie points. It allows you to build circuits without soldering.
part_guide.uno: An Arduino Uno microcontroller board. It executes the night light logic and controls the components.
part_guide.ldr: A photoresistor (LDR) with a small circular face marked with a squiggly track. It senses light intensity.
part_guide.r_ldr: A 10 kΩ resistor with brown, black, and orange color bands. It forms a voltage divider circuit with the photoresistor.
part_guide.led_yellow: A 5 mm yellow LED with a long positive leg (anode) and short negative leg (cathode). It emits light when activated.
part_guide.r_led: A 220 Ω resistor with red, red, and brown color bands. It prevents the LED from burning out.
part_guide.w_gnd_rail: A black jumper wire. It distributes common electrical ground from the Arduino GND pin to the top rail.
part_guide.w_5v: A red jumper wire. It supplies 5 volts of power from the Arduino to one leg of the photoresistor.
part_guide.w_a0: A blue jumper wire. It carries the variable voltage signal from the light sensor to Arduino pin A0.
part_guide.w_ldr_gnd: A black jumper wire. It connects the 10 kΩ resistor to the top ground rail.
part_guide.w_led_sig: A yellow jumper wire. It sends positive switching voltage from digital pin 9 to the LED.
part_guide.w_led_gnd: A black jumper wire. It connects the LED's 220 Ω resistor to the top ground rail to complete the circuit.
